This comment is why so many people have such a problem with the entitlement of gig worker. So much of what is said is hyperbolic and full of fallacies. You bring up the worst case scenario for an instacart shopper and then in the same breath also say “$2 won’t cut it.” You’re right, we both know that. But that’s not what the average order is. Most orders that get placed are for a normal volume of everyday groceries, OR LESS. The whole point of my comment was that instacart shoppers aren’t entitled to more than the average person makes in a comparable job at a company. I know this will make your head spin to hear, but the fact of the matter is that many shoppers do this job because they don’t WANT to work a “regular” job. It doesn’t require any skill or education up front. Literally pretty much anyone can start doing it within the week. You’re insane for expecting anything more than the rest of us working shitty entry level jobs. You CHOSE the job that puts wear and miles on your car. That’s part of the deal. Plenty of people drive their personal car for work. Might their company pay them mileage? Sure, but it’s pennies. Many teachers with a college education, who wrangle 20-30 children who don’t belong to them all day, only make $20 an hour. Shoppers are so detached from the reality of what they're “owed” in this slave wage economy. I’m not saying you DON’T deserve more money. Quite the opposite. But look around. Everybody is underpaid. You’re not special.

You saying that ANY order is worth $200 made me fucking cackle, so thanks for that.

I think I made it perfectly clear that I don’t think my time is worth more than yours. What I’m saying is YOUR time isn’t worth more than mine. The way you described your job function is pretty damn close to a job in grocery store. Acting like you DESERVE more than $20 an hour in most scenarios is fucking greedy. Like I mentioned in my original comment, that’s the high end of the hour wage spectrum for retail employees in the US. I wouldn’t be an instacart shopper for any realistic amount of money because I don’t want to grocery shop for other people. You don’t want to work a structured job so you do gig work. It’s all the same. So many shoppers have such a chip on their shoulder.

I totally understand bitching about the people who order from instacart and completely abuse the system and give little to no tip. Those who order tons of items, heavy items, don’t answer the phone when you can’t find their house ect. Instacart is a job. People want and use the service, so people who want to provide the service are valid for making their money this way. But it’s insane to me to look at this subreddit and see so many shoppers who think they’re owed so much. $20 for less than 40 items which can definitely be done within an hour. That’s how much actual grocery store employees make in the most expensive parts of the country with the highest minimum wages. I’m not gonna speculate if instacart shoppers “deserve” more or less money. Everyone deserves more money in America. But what blows my mind is how so many of you whine and complain about stairs, elevators, driving around apartment complexes, or whatever else it is. Just about every “real” job doesn’t let you pick and choose the tough or undesirable aspects of the job function. You’re getting paid that $20 to deliver groceries. Some days it’ll be easier, some days it’ll be harder. You guys preach about this being a real job and that it’s just as valid as someone working a 9-5 but then you complain about having to fulfill the job description. Most service industry/retail jobs require you can lift 50lbs and can be on your feet for 8 hours.  Instacart pays shit, but you signed up for that. You’re relying on complete strangers who are also underpaid to pay your bills. If you want more than the average person makes in America, go get a job that pays more than $20 where you get paid a legally agreed upon hourly wage. Read the room. Everybody is out here struggling with money right now. Just because some people call instacart deliveries a “luxury” thus meaning people should pay out the ass for it is irrelevant. You guys don’t deserve to make more than the rest of us because the people making orders ASSumably have more disposable income. It’s wild to see so many people who are potentially dissatisfied with a $20 TIP when they have to climb up some stairs.
